rules_evaluated.rule_lead: **Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go. Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.**
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read prompt-only: apt101-d2-what-ran-overnight enforces 'each quoted exactly' and "Don't comment on how they compare"; apt101-d2-mark-the-doubt enforces 'put the source's own sentence next to the digest's line... If the source doesn't say it, say so plainly'; apt101-d2-ask-the-other-way enforces the reversal branch ('Support only') and 'Add nothing'. Closest body script: L31 'Push back if the list comes back as a summary of the digest' - an optional push-back in suggestion register (carve-out), not a count-script; L45 'If your doubt lands on a typo, look again.' is a calibration. Harm (forcing function explained in prose instead of enacted by the fence) absent: the mechanism is not named in the body at all, per maintainer L87.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: **Classroom = default delivery; body teaches work, trainer manages room.**
rules_evaluated.evidence: Authored room conversation in the body: L33 'read its name aloud to the other two and say what let it through'; L47-55 Phase 3 'Laptops half shut. Each of you reads your four lines to the other two ... Then ask, of each person's digest in turn: - Is the headline the one you expected? - Did it find what your line asked for?'; L64 'Each of you reads your two headlines aloud'; L70 'Each of you reads your doubt and its reason. Together, pick...'. Phase 3 is a read-aloud-and-question round whose output is no shared artefact (each person's own four lines), so it is not the 'designed content of a group round' that sibling APT101 exercises cite; Phase 5 is a real group decision with a named artefact (team/doubts.md) and is fine. Third carve-out allows one room-naming line per file; this file has four room-mechanics cues. Second carve-out (sanctioned human slot) needs a dated accept-note: accept_notes_found holds only the Quality stamp (L80). Harm the rule prevents (body scripting pacing/compare/share the trainer owns) is partly present in L51-55; the questions themselves are the work (maintainer L87 hidden-spine thread 1), which is why this is non-blocking.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Maintainer call: add a dated accept-note naming the sanctioned-slot carve-out for Phase 3 and 5, or move the two-question script and the L33 read-aloud to trainer notes and keep the questions in a prompt.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Contract (strategy storyline step 3): the overnight digest agrees with the favourite hypothesis, fluently; Day 2 is that unease, with the rescue (team rules) after. Leaves the student unsure which digest line to trust and equipped to mark one. Closest to resolving early: L76 'Each of you still knew one source well enough to catch where it went past what was there.' - names a competence, does not declare any doubt settled or the digest sound, and hands the chosen doubt to the outcome pick. Setup beat (L1-21) mood-exempt per carve-out. Teaching beats 8/8(P1)/8/7/9/8, close 8; P3 at 7 is the facilitator-premium signature (two-question script flattens a good reveal), not below 7.

grep -niE 'fabricat|hallucin|violation|messed|ashamed|wrong|mistake' on body L1-76 -> 1 hit, L41 'Not the one that is plainly wrong; the one you would least want a priority call to rest on.' It steers the pick AWAY from error-catching toward not-knowing; L39 'The agent read them once.' puts the gap on the agent, not on the student. Unease stays 'I can't tell which line to trust'.

H1 'Read the digest' and phase headers 'See what ran', 'Mark the line you trust least', 'Ask it the other way round', 'Pick the doubt' name practices. Closest failure-word: 'doubt' (L66 'Pick the doubt'), which is the discipline's object (a marked, sourced doubt), not a failure label like fabrication or hallucination.

Facets: (front-run) body names no mechanism; the kind of line (support/test/both) is not named before the rerun at L60 (maintainer L87: 'Nothing before the rerun names what kind of line it was. apt101-why-it-agreed names it after beat 3'), and grep for M[0-9]/Module N on body = 0. (arc) opens from Day 1's send-off artefacts (latest.html, expect.md, what-goes-in.md, bet.md) and closes at L76 handing one chosen doubt to the outcome pick (maintainer L83). (Big Idea) Day 2 turn: digest fluent, student knows one source; the rescue (team rules, Keep-and-run-tonight) is not pre-empted. (mood-resolve) no verification step settles the doubt: L72 'That is a team call, not a vote, and nobody's agent makes it.' Teaching moment (judge-owned, not a rule row): Phase 4 reversal fires for every seat via the prompt's two-branch rule (L60-62), so a persona cannot skip it; lands.
